_comment: Task instructions for SHORT-SPAN units, where the marked span is a bare topic noun phrase (a SQuAD title) rather than a passage. Constraints: each must (a) make sense for any SQuAD-title type -- place, country, animal phylum, instrument, building, historical period, social class; (b) be answerable from the model's own parametric knowledge, since there is no passage to read; (c) NOT be a copy/transcribe task (those belong to copy_injected, where the target is the span verbatim); (d) terminate naturally, so targets end with finish_reason=stop. NOTE: a 'suggest three books or articles' template was removed during validation -- it invites citation hallucination and induced a degenerate repetition loop ('J. C. H. H. H...') on 2 of 3 test titles. Do not add tasks that ask the model to name sources it cannot retrieve. Generate targets at max_new>=1024: the longest legitimate target measured 2123 chars, within 4% of a 512-token cap.
tasks: Give a one-sentence description of the topic.
Suggest three related search queries for the topic given.
Write a short encyclopedia-style opening paragraph for the topic.
List three facts about the topic.
Name three subtopics someone studying this topic should read about.
Explain the topic to a ten-year-old in two or three sentences.
Write a single-sentence definition suitable for a glossary.
Give two reasons the topic might interest a historian.
Suggest a title for a short documentary about the topic.
List three questions a curious reader might ask about the topic.
Write a one-line summary suitable for a search-result snippet.
Name the field of study most closely associated with the topic.
Give three keywords that would help catalogue the topic in a library.
Write two sentences explaining why the topic matters.
Write a short note on what distinguishes the topic from similar things.
List two common misconceptions about the topic.
Write a short caption for a photograph of the topic.
Name three things commonly associated with the topic.
Give a brief note about when the topic became significant.
Write a one-paragraph overview of the topic for a general audience.
Suggest three tags for an article about the topic.
Name two topics that are frequently confused with this one.
Write an opening sentence for a magazine article about the topic.
List three aspects of the topic worth further research.
Give a two-sentence answer to the question "what is this?" about the topic.
Suggest an appropriate category for the topic in an online encyclopedia.
Write a short quiz question about the topic, followed by its answer.
Name three terms a newcomer to the topic would need to learn.
Describe in two sentences where someone would encounter the topic.
Write a concise summary of the topic in under thirty words.
Give one detail about the topic that a casual reader might not know.
Suggest three related topics for a "see also" section.
Write a one-sentence introduction for a lecture on the topic.
List two reasons the topic is studied.
Name the broader category the topic belongs to, and explain the connection in one sentence.
Give a short factual note about the topic's origin.
Write a brief description of the topic for a museum label.
Suggest two questions for an interview with an expert on the topic.
Provide a short overview of the topic in three bullet points.
Write a two-sentence note on how the topic is commonly represented in popular culture.
